In this section we spell out what the results in
Section <REF_0001>
mean for deformations of algebraic spaces.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. Let <MATH_0002> be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over <MATH_0003>. The following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0004> is a thickening of algebraic spaces as defined
in More on Morphisms of Spaces, Section
<REF_0001>, and
<STRUCT_0003> the associated morphism
<MATH_0005>
of ringed topoi (Properties of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0002>)
is a thickening in the sense of
Section <REF_0003>.
<STRUCT_0004>

We stress that this is not a triviality.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Assume (1). By More on Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0001>
the morphism <MATH_0001> induces an equivalence of small <ACCENT_0001>tale
sites and in particular of topoi. Of course <MATH_0002>
is surjective with locally nilpotent kernel by definition
of thickenings.

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>
Assume (2). (This direction is less important and more of
a curiosity.) For any <ACCENT_0002>tale morphism <MATH_0003> we see
that <MATH_0004> has the same <ACCENT_0003>tale topos
as <MATH_0005>. In particular, <MATH_0006> is quasi-compact if and only if
<MATH_0007> is quasi-compact because being quasi-compact
is a topos theoretic notion (Sites, Lemma <REF_0002>).
Having said this we see that <MATH_0008> is quasi-compact and quasi-separated
if and only if <MATH_0009> is quasi-compact and quasi-separated
(because you can characterize <MATH_0010> being quasi-separated by saying
that for all <MATH_0011> quasi-compact algebraic spaces <ACCENT_0004>tale over <MATH_0012>
we have that <MATH_0013> is quasi-compact).
